projects/worldlogic-1.21.1-neoforge/src/.comparison: Vanilla clay uses fine low-contrast mineral patches; the silt uses similarly quiet transitions in tan, with short interrupted beds instead of the former parallel bands.

findings.silhouette: Fine compact sediment rather than raised stones or granular dirt.
findings.cluster_structure: Short flattened deposits interlock with smaller irregular midtone gaps; center gray lens is embedded.
findings.micro_contrast: Light tan edges around upper-left deposit turn into adjacent ochre midtone rather than white accents.
findings.light_and_volume: Low relief indicated by a narrow pale upper plane on each major sediment body and a muted edge below.
findings.material_continuity: Warm mineral base remains continuous through gray sediment inclusion around x7–10, y7–8.
findings.edge_variation: Broken short beds terminate at different offsets, avoiding uninterrupted horizontal stripes.
findings.variant_identity: Tan fine sediment has flatter, less contrasty structure than loam and humus.
findings.vanilla_comparison: Vanilla clay comparison at native size shows restrained tonal differences, with warm silt rather than blue clay.
findings.aggregate_structure: Elongated small mineral aggregates vary in length and neighboring value.
findings.tile_rhythm: 3x3 tiled review shows short recurring beds but no uninterrupted hard seam or full-width stripe.

projects/worldlogic-1.21.1-neoforge/src/.comparison: Rooted dirt preserves brown earth around organic inclusions; frozen soil similarly keeps its host readable, replacing former broad pale blobs with narrow desaturated icy fissures. Snow is a cool-value reference, not a copied white palette.

findings.silhouette: Brown compact earth remains the predominant surface; ice reads as seams within it.
findings.cluster_structure: Several earth clods interlock with short irregular frost lenses, including a branching upper-left seam.
findings.micro_contrast: Muted gray-green transition pixels surround small pale blue cores.
findings.light_and_volume: The ice center is brighter than its shaded boundary; brown clods have shallow upper highlights.
findings.material_continuity: Frost occupies a small fraction of the soil and stays bounded by neutral intermediate pixels.
findings.edge_variation: Upper-left branch, right lens, lower-left wedge and bottom fissure have different contours.
findings.variant_identity: Distinguishes frozen soil by cold inclusions and cooler earth, not by painting the entire surface white.
findings.vanilla_comparison: Rooted dirt and snow viewed at equal native scale show useful embedded contrast and cool ramp behavior respectively.
findings.aggregate_structure: Clods retain earthy irregular dark recesses while ice follows interstitial gaps.
findings.tile_rhythm: Repeated tile keeps the soil base continuous; frost shapes recur at block cadence but do not form broad white spots.

projects/worldlogic-1.21.1-neoforge/src/.comparison: Compared to actual dirt, the warm brown palette and small embedded gray particle retain material continuity while narrower dark cavities and varied clod edges give humus a darker organic appearance without the old flat repeated pattern.

findings.silhouette: Irregular earth crumbs read as friable organic soil rather than cobblestone.
findings.cluster_structure: Primary aggregates vary in size; small dark recesses separate the clods around the upper center and lower center.
findings.micro_contrast: A few warm highlights mark turning planes, with mid-brown adjacent pixels mediating the contrast.
findings.light_and_volume: Highlights on the upper edge of selected clods contrast with dark crevices instead of uniform pillow shading.
findings.material_continuity: Brown base is close to vanilla dirt; one subdued gray inclusion is contained within a clod boundary.
findings.edge_variation: Clods are nonidentical and several cross the tile edges rather than ending in a straight frame.
findings.variant_identity: Darker and more crumbly than loam; no pale ice or sediment lenses.
findings.vanilla_comparison: At 1x and enlarged scale the new warm brown ramp sits closer to dirt than the old flat four-color pattern.
findings.aggregate_structure: Small connected soil crumbs with visible interstitial shadows, especially center and bottom.
findings.tile_rhythm: 3x3 tiling shows no rectangular frame; adjoining vanilla dirt retains a compatible brown hue although a horizon contrast remains.

projects/worldlogic-1.21.1-neoforge/src/.comparison: The actual vanilla dirt reference is more contrasty and stone-speckled; loam retains its brown identity with brighter ochre planes and smaller, shallower crevices instead of a recolor of humus.

findings.silhouette: Friable warm mineral soil formed by flatter angular crumb faces.
findings.cluster_structure: Several broad light planes and dark irregular seams interlock; one small gray fragment lies at the right center.
findings.micro_contrast: Restrained tan highlights and adjacent orange-brown transitions soften the individual aggregate boundaries.
findings.light_and_volume: Light along selected upper edges creates low relief; recessed pixels are localized instead of outlining every clod.
findings.material_continuity: Warm continuous brown background surrounds one small mineral-colored fragment.
findings.edge_variation: Clods at upper-left, middle and lower-right have different widths and contours.
findings.variant_identity: Lighter ochre and shallower cavities separate loam from dark humus and peat.
findings.vanilla_comparison: Native-scale comparison with dirt retains earthy orange hue while reducing its strong dark mottling.
findings.aggregate_structure: Mineral crumbs and shallow recesses suggest a mixed sand/clay soil rather than packed stones.
findings.tile_rhythm: 3x3 tiled preview retains a quiet repeated ground rhythm; edge clods cross tile boundaries and no black border occurs.

projects/worldlogic-1.21.1-neoforge/src/.comparison: Vanilla mud establishes a dark wet material and rooted dirt provides embedded organic cues; peat uses brown-black recesses with muted short fibers rather than gray mud or the old diagonal bands.

findings.silhouette: Dark compressed organic clods, with sparse root-like traces visible on the surface.
findings.cluster_structure: Short fibers cross several irregular flattened clods and interrupt the darker cavities.
findings.micro_contrast: Warm brown tips contrast locally against deep charcoal-brown recesses without bright isolated stone specks.
findings.light_and_volume: Selective upper-plane brown accents give compressed material shallow relief.
findings.material_continuity: Dark earth stays continuous and the fiber tones remain within its brown material family.
findings.edge_variation: Short crooked traces change direction and length rather than extending across the whole block.
findings.variant_identity: Peat is darker and more fibrous than humus; no mineral-gray inclusion or pale frost.
findings.vanilla_comparison: Same-scale mud comparison shows similar low overall brightness but a warmer and more organic structure.
findings.aggregate_structure: Interlocked dark clumps have compressed fiber-like edges and shadowed gaps.
findings.tile_rhythm: 3x3 repeat has a dark coherent rhythm; there are no straight full-width stripe seams.
